concerns.text: Task T005 hardcodes `token_limit` to 100000, violating FR-002 and Spec Assumptions which mandate `[deferred]` for the token count. The task must not silently resolve a deferred empirical value; it must initialize the config to the `[deferred]` marker or a placeholder that forces the validation script (T002-CHK) to fail until the value is explicitly set in the spec.

Task T012-IMPL implements N=5 generation for the training loss proxy. This creates a semantic weakening of Constitution Principle VII (Resource-Constrained Architectural Fidelity) and the Spec's 120-minute training budget. Generating 5 full forward passes per batch on a 2-CPU runner will exceed the time budget, effectively failing the 'Independent Test' in US-01. The task must either reduce N (weakening the proxy) or the spec must be updated to allow a larger budget; as written, the task guarantees a violation of the resource constraint.

Task T019a attempts to fetch a non-existent 'self_consistency' dataset. FR-003 mandates generating 10 paths for the 'Self-Consistency benchmark'. The task fails to define the derivation logic (e.g., 'generate N=10 paths for GSM8K test set') required to satisfy the spec's intent without a pre-existing artifact, risking implementation failure and violating the requirement to produce the benchmark data.

Tasks T074, T076, T077, T079, and T081 introduce new metrics ('Behavioral Adaptation', 'Computational Cost', 'Efficiency Ratio', 'Prediction Penalty', 'Novelty Detection') not defined in FR-001 through FR-007 or SC-001 through SC-005. This constitutes silent scope expansion (weakening the spec's defined success criteria) and violates the principle that tasks must not introduce unverified empirical values or metrics not mandated by the spec.

Task T004-IMPL loads the *entire* Pile train split and filters for 'arXiv' prefixes. FR-002 and Constitution Principle VII require training on a 100k-token subset. Loading millions of tokens before truncation violates the 7GB RAM and 2-hour budget constraints, creating a semantic violation of the resource fidelity requirement.
